message.content:
Pantone doesn’t have a single “official” code called *Sky Blue*—the brand offers several light‑to‑medium blues that designers often refer to informally as sky blue. Below are three common Pantone matches that most people think of when they picture a classic sky‑blue hue:

| # | Pantone Code | Description / Typical Use |
|---|--------------|---------------------------|
| **A** | **Pantone 290 C** | A very pale, almost pastel sky blue – great for backgrounds, soft accents, and airy designs. |
| **B** | **Pantone 292 C** | Slightly brighter than 290 C but still gentle; used frequently in fashion prints and corporate branding where you want a clean, uplifting feel. |
| **C** | **Pantone 295 C** | A deeper, slightly more saturated sky blue that works well for logos, signage, and print materials needing a bit more visual weight while staying within the “sky” family. |

If you’re working from a physical swatch library, look under the “Blue” section near the top of the Pantone guide—they’ll usually list all the sky‑like tones together. If you only see one entry labelled “Sky Blue,” it’s likely either 290 C or 292 C depending on your version of the guide.  

Feel free to let me know which context you’re designing for (print vs digital, mood board, etc.) so I can narrow down the best match!
